definitions.gloss: grilled mutton dish of Hokkaido; Genghis Khan barbecue
definitions.explanation: Slices of mutton or lamb grilled with vegetables on a dome-shaped iron skillet and dipped in a soy-based sauce. The best-known local dish of Hokkaido, eaten at restaurants, at beer gardens, and outdoors.

examples.japanese: {北海道|ほっかいどう}でジンギスカンを{食|た}べた。
ジンギスカン{鍋|なべ}で{羊肉|ようにく}と{野菜|やさい}を{焼|や}く。
examples.english: You grill the mutton and vegetables on a jingisukan skillet.

examples.japanese: {札幌|さっぽろ}では{花見|はなみ}の{季節|きせつ}に{公園|こうえん}でジンギスカンを{楽|たの}しむ{人|ひと}も{多|おお}い。
examples.english: In Sapporo, many people enjoy jingisukan in the parks during cherry-blossom season.

notes:
Named after ジンギスカン, the Japanese form of Genghis Khan; the link to the Mongol ruler is a marketing legend rather than history. The dish itself dates from early twentieth-century Hokkaido, where sheep were raised for wool.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ジンギスカン{鍋|なべ}: the dome-shaped skillet used for the dish (also the dish itself)
- ジンギスカンを{食|た}べに{行|い}く: to go out for jingisukan
- {生|なま}ラムのジンギスカン: jingisukan made with fresh (unfrozen) lamb

CULTURAL NOTE:
The curved skillet lets the fat run down to the vegetables at the rim while the meat cooks on top. In Hokkaido, outdoor jingisukan at {花見|はなみ} or beer gardens is as ordinary as a barbecue elsewhere in Japan.
